topics: 👑 The Emperor and King Shapur — Rabbi Yehoshua and Shmuel plant a dream by daytime suggestion
💰 Bar Haddaya — the interpreter who read the same dream as blessing for Abaye and curse for Rava
⚖️ Rava's Curse — 'all dreams follow the mouth', exile to Rome, and bar Haddaya's end
🧩 Sages as Interpreters — Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, and the heretic's confessions
📜 Preempt the Bad Verse — Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's rule for rivers, birds, pots, and more
🐂 Dream Symbols — the five things said of an ox, donkeys, cats, grapes, horses, camels, and elephants

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Bar Haddaya and the Power of the Interpreter
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 56a–56b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with two kings who dreamed exactly what a sage told them they would see, proving that dreams come from daytime thoughts. Then comes the long story of bar Haddaya, who interpreted identical dreams favorably for Abaye, who paid, and disastrously for Rava, who did not — until Rava found the interpreter's book reading 'all dreams follow the mouth' and cursed him. Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi show how sages decode dream images, including a heretic whose every dream exposed a sin. The second amud lists symbols with double meanings and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's advice: rise early and recite the good verse before the bad one can take hold.

slides.title: 💰 One Dream, Two Readings: Bar Haddaya's Ledger
slides.subtitle: Abaye paid a zuz; Rava did not — and the same images split into opposite fates
rows: 'Your ox shall be slain before your eyes' (Deut. 28:31)
Your business will profit; you won't be able to eat from joy
Your business will fail; you won't be able to eat from grief
'You shall have olive trees throughout your borders' (Deut. 28:40)
Read from the end: 'your olives shall drop off'
'All the peoples of the earth shall see…' (Deut. 28:10)
Your name will go out as head of the yeshiva
The king's treasury will be robbed and you will be seized as a thief — and it happened the next day
Lettuce on the mouth of barrels
Your business will double like lettuce
Your business will be bitter like lettuce
A barrel hanging from a palm tree
Your business will rise like a palm
Your goods will be sweet like dates — cheap
A donkey foal braying at our heads
You will be 'king' with an amora standing beside you
The word peter ḥamor is erased from your tefillin — the vav, he insisted

callout.label: Alone with Rava:
callout.text: A fallen outer door — your wife will die. Teeth falling out — your children will die. Two flying doves — you will divorce two women. Two turnip heads — two blows with a club. That day two blind men fighting struck Rava twice; when they raised their staffs again he said, 'Enough, I only saw two.'

slides.title: ⚖️ The Fall of Bar Haddaya
slides.subtitle: Rava pays, the readings flip, and the interpreter's own book condemns him

nodes.content: 💵 Rava finally pays. Now a fallen wall = property without limit; Abaye's house collapsing on him = Abaye's yeshiva will come to you; his own house's bricks carried off = your teachings spread through the world; the Egyptian Hallel = miracles will be done for you
📕 On a ship, bar Haddaya's book falls. Rava reads in it: כׇּל הַחֲלוֹמוֹת הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הַפֶּה. 'Scoundrel! It all depended on you, and you caused me such pain'
😡 Rava forgives everything except the daughter of Rav Ḥisda, his wife: 'May this man be delivered to a kingdom that has no mercy on him'
🚶 Bar Haddaya: the curse of a sage comes true even when baseless, all the more so Rava's, which was just. 'The Master said: exile atones for sin' — he flees to Rome

columns.label: The wardrobe keeper
columns.content: A needle in my finger; a worm between two fingers — 'give me a zuz.' No coin, no answer. A worm over the whole hand — 'a worm has eaten all the silks!'

columns.label: The verdict
columns.content: The keeper, about to be executed: 'Bring the one who knew and did not say.' Because of your zuz the king's silks were ruined

nodes.content: ☠️ Two cedars bent together with a rope, a leg tied to each, the rope released — bar Haddaya split in two

callout.label: The lesson:
callout.text: An interpreter who sells outcomes for a fee is not a bystander; when he withholds a reading for want of a coin, the ruin that follows is charged to him.

slides.title: 🧩 Sages Decode the Image
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi read dreams by wordplay and association

lines.speaker: Ben Dama
lines.text: I saw my two cheeks fall off.

lines.speaker: R' Yishmael
lines.text: Two Roman battalions plotted evil against you, and they died.

lines.speaker: Bar Kappara
lines.text: My nose fell off. My two hands were cut off. My two legs were cut off. They told me I would die in Adar and not see Nisan.

lines.speaker: Rabbi
lines.text: Anger (ḥaron af) has left you. You will not need the labor of your hands. You ride a horse. You will die in glory (adruta) and not come to temptation (nissayon).

lines.speaker: A heretic
lines.text: I was watering olives with oil. I plucked a star, then swallowed it. My eyes kissed each other. I kissed the moon. I was peeling eggs.

lines.speaker: R' Yishmael
lines.text: You had relations with your mother. You kidnapped an Israelite and sold him, spending the money. Relations with your sister. With an Israelite's wife. You strip the dead — and a woman arrived to say the cloak he wore belonged to a man who had died.

lines.speaker: The heretic
lines.text: They said my father left me property in Cappadocia — but I have none there and he never went.

lines.speaker: R' Yishmael
lines.text: Kappa is a beam, deka is ten. Look at the tenth beam of your house. It was full of coins.

callout.label: Notice:
callout.text: Every image is decoded through a symbol the Gemara already uses: Israel as stars, siblings as two eyes, a woman as the moon, the egg of the mourner's meal. The heretic admitted all were true except the last — until the evidence walked in.

slides.title: 📜 Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Say the Good Verse First
slides.subtitle: For images that Scripture uses both ways, rise early and recite the favorable verse before the other can 'precede' it

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Ḥanan: three signs of peace — a river ('I will extend peace to her like a river', Isa. 66:12), a bird ('as birds hovering', Isa. 31:5), a pot ('You will establish [tishpot] peace', Isa. 26:12). Rabbi Ḥanina: only a pot without meat — with meat it is Micah 3:3
2️⃣ But each has a dark verse too: 'distress will come in like a river' (Isa. 59:19), 'a bird that wanders from her nest' (Prov. 27:8), 'set on the pot' (Ezek. 24:3) — so recite the good one first

3️⃣ Grapes: 'like grapes in the wilderness' (Hos. 9:10) before 'grapes of gall' (Deut. 32:32). A mountain: 'how beautiful upon the mountains' (Isa. 52:7) before 'for the mountains I will weep' (Jer. 9:9)

4️⃣ A shofar: the great shofar of ingathering (Isa. 27:13) before the war horn of Giva (Hos. 5:8). A dog: 'no dog shall whet his tongue' (Ex. 11:7) before 'the dogs are greedy' (Isa. 56:11). A lion: 'the lion has roared' (Amos 3:8) before 'a lion is gone up from his thicket' (Jer. 4:7)

5️⃣ A shave: Joseph 'shaved and changed his raiment' (Gen. 41:14) before Samson's 'if I be shaven my strength will go' (Judges 16:17). A well: 'a well of living waters' (Song 4:15) before Jer. 6:7. A reed: 'a bruised reed he shall not break' (Isa. 42:3) before 'the staff of this bruised reed' (II Kings 18:21)
6️⃣ An ox: 'his firstling bullock, majesty is his' (Deut. 33:17) before 'if an ox gore a man' (Ex. 21:28)

callout.label: Why a well is good:
callout.text: Rabbi Ḥanina: one who sees a well sees peace (Gen. 26:19). Rabbi Natan: he has found Torah, for 'whoever finds me finds life' (Prov. 8:35) matches 'a well of living water'. Rava: actual life.

slides.title: 🐂 A Field Guide to Dream Symbols
slides.subtitle: Baraitot and amoraic sayings on the second amud

boxes.title: Good Omens
items: A reed (kaneh): expect wisdom — 'get [kene] wisdom'; reeds: understanding (Prov. 4:7)
Rabbi Zeira: pumpkin, heart of palm, wax and reed are all good; a pumpkin is shown only to one who fears Heaven with all his might
A donkey: expect salvation — 'lowly, and riding upon a donkey' (Zech. 9:9)
A white horse, walking or running; a red horse walking
Ishmael son of Abraham (not any Arab): your prayer is heard; Pinehas: a wonder will be done for you

boxes.title: The Ox: Five Things
items: Ate its flesh — you will become wealthy
It gored you — sons who 'gore' each other in Torah
It bit you — suffering is coming
It kicked you — a long journey
You rode it — you rise to greatness; but 'rode it — he will die' refers to the ox riding him

boxes.title: It Depends
items: A cat: where it is called shunra, a nice song (shira na'a); where shinra, a change for the worse (shinui ra)
White grapes: always good; black grapes: good in season, bad out of season
A camel (gamal): death was decreed and he was spared — 'I will also surely bring you up [gam alo]' (Gen. 46:4), or 'the Lord also [gam] has put away your sin' (II Sam. 12:13)
An elephant (pil): wonders (pelaot) — yet a baraita excludes elephant and monkey from good animal dreams; 'not difficult…'

callout.label: Open question:
callout.text: The daf ends mid-resolution: the elephant that brings wonders and the elephant excluded from good omens must be different cases. The distinction is stated on the next daf.

summary.principle: A dream is raw material: it is planted by daytime thought and finished by the mouth that interprets it, so choose the interpreter and the verse with care.

flowSteps.content: 👑 The emperor and King Shapur dream exactly what Rabbi Yehoshua and Shmuel told them — dreams follow the day's thoughts
💰 Bar Haddaya reads identical dreams as profit for Abaye (paid) and ruin for Rava (unpaid); the predictions come true
⚖️ Rava finds 'all dreams follow the mouth' in his book, curses him; bar Haddaya exiles himself to Rome and is executed for withholding a reading over a zuz

columns.content: 🧩 Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi decode images through wordplay — cheeks, nose, hands, stars, moon, the tenth beam
📜 Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: rise early and recite the good verse for river, bird, pot, grapes, mountain, shofar, dog, lion, shave, well, reed, ox

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: the same image can carry a blessing or a curse; the interpretation, and the verse you speak first, decides which

quiz.q: How did Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Ḥananya make the emperor see a specific dream?
o: He prayed for it during the Priestly Blessing
He described the scene to him, and the emperor thought about it all day and saw it that night
He had it interpreted before three people
He wrote the dream in a book the emperor read
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua told the emperor he would see the Persians enslave him; the emperor thought about it the whole day and dreamed it that night. Shmuel did the same with King Shapur.

quiz.q: What determined whether bar Haddaya interpreted a dream favorably or unfavorably?
o: Whether the dreamer was a Torah scholar
Whether the dream occurred in the morning
Whether the dreamer paid him a fee
Whether the dream quoted a verse from Deuteronomy
quiz.e: Bar Haddaya interpreted favorably for one who paid and unfavorably for one who did not; Abaye paid and Rava did not, so the same dreams received opposite readings.

quiz.q: What did Rava find written in bar Haddaya's book, and why did it enrage him?
o: A list of his debts, which he had never been told about
'All dreams follow the mouth' — proving the calamities had depended on the interpreter's choice
The name of the thief who robbed the king's treasury
A curse written against Rava's household
quiz.e: The book said 'all dreams follow the mouth'; Rava realized his suffering had been in bar Haddaya's hands, forgave everything except the prediction about his wife, and cursed him.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, what should one do after dreaming of a river, bird, or pot?
o: Fast the next day
Rise early and recite the verse with the favorable meaning before the negative verse can precede it
Tell the dream only to a paid interpreter
Recite the blessing 'Who makes creatures different'
quiz.e: Since these images appear in Scripture in both good and bad contexts, one should rise early and recite the good verse, such as 'I will extend peace to her like a river', before the negative verse can take effect.

quiz.q: The baraita lists five things about an ox in a dream. How does the Gemara reconcile 'riding it — he rises to greatness' with another baraita, 'riding it — he will die'?
o: One refers to a white ox and the other to a red ox
One refers to a scholar and the other to an ignoramus
One refers to a man riding the ox, the other to the ox riding the man
One refers to a dream in the morning and the other at night
quiz.e: The Gemara answers 'not difficult': when he rides the ox he rises to greatness; when the ox rides him it is a sign of death.
